about.title: What is Frontier Ops?
paragraphs: Frontier Ops is an original strategy sandbox concept created for this template. Begin with a small settlement, establish reliable supplies, recruit a workforce, and choose when to extend your border. The sample setting turns each round into an exercise in planning: balance growth, protection, and the cost of holding new ground before committing your reserves.

This Frontier Codex demonstrates the structure of a complete guide site without pretending that a complete game database exists. The visible building, doctrine, and news records are editorial previews. The opening guide is the complete playable reading path; every preview remains clearly marked until its own content is ready.

buildings.title: Builder Lodge
buildings.description: A Builder Lodge represents construction capacity in the demo setting. Prioritise a reliable build crew before filling every plot with low-yield structures. Extra capacity helps the entire settlement respond when the next decision changes your plan.

buildings.title: Supply Depot
buildings.description: A shared collection point keeps the industrial district organised. Place it near the working cluster so your supply route stays short, then expand around that centre. This preview shows how support infrastructure can make every other plot more useful.

buildings.title: Aerial Outpost
buildings.description: The Aerial Outpost is a mid-game response concept, designed to extend reach once an economy can support replacement costs. Build a dependable reserve before planning an attack. A mobile force only helps when the settlement behind it remains stable.

strategies.title: Steady Growth
strategies.description: Put the supply network ahead of an early army. Build dependable income, keep a small reserve, and only switch into mobile defense when the settlement can replace losses. The demo plan favours consistent progress and leaves room to react to the map.

strategies.title: Sky Patrol · Rapid Response
strategies.description: Trade some long-term growth for an earlier response window. Keep the opening compact, identify an exposed approach, and prepare a mobile patrol before the frontier gets crowded. The right timing matters more than filling every available unit slot.

strategies.title: Fortified Frontier
strategies.description: Keep the working district behind a compact perimeter, protect the housing zone, and allow reserves to accumulate. A slower opening can pay off if the settlement survives pressure without replacing its workforce. The plan turns safe production into a later opportunity.

news.title: Mobile response briefing — when an aerial outpost fits the opening plan
news.description: A resilient supply network comes before expensive mobility. This preview outlines the questions to ask before committing to a rapid response force and the reserve that makes such a decision sustainable.

purpose.title: A frontier field manual built around clear decisions
paragraphs: A useful guide should explain the decision behind a build order, not just list purchases. This original demo follows that idea: distinguish an opening priority from a later option, explain the reserve that protects the plan, and keep draft material visibly separate from a complete guide.

Use the site as a reading path and a future reference. Start with the complete opening briefing, then explore the preview cards to see the planned topics. Their layout preserves the depth of a full codex while their status makes clear which material is already available.

faq.title: Frontier Ops at a glance
items: What kind of game is Frontier Ops?
An original country-building sandbox concept used to demonstrate this template. Its economy, structures, and defensive plans are illustrative rather than verified mechanics from a released title.
Are there any working reward codes?
No. This fictional concept has no live game, redemption system, or rewards. The codes entry is an editorial preview and makes no claim that a reward can be collected.
Where should a new reader begin?
The opening briefing is the complete guide in this demo. It introduces the planning loop, a ten-step opening, and the habits that help you keep an expanding settlement manageable.

guides.title: Frontier Ops guides
guides.description: Long-form field reports for a country-building sandbox concept. Opening orders, supply planning, and the small decisions that help a fragile outpost become a dependable settlement.
paragraphs: Each complete guide in this codex is written as a practical reading path rather than a quick collection of tips. The opening briefing follows a settlement from its first production plot to a stable defensive position, with clear decision points and a reserve-minded approach. Start there if this is your first visit; the remaining topics are clearly marked previews of the planned library.

The preview records introduce future structure references and strategic choices without claiming that those pages already exist. Use the complete opening guide for the finished example. The broader doctrine cards show how a larger codex would connect buildings, systems, and long-form field reports.
